tweets.text:
Electricity's evolution provides a perfect metaphor for AI's coming transformation. What began as simple light bulbs (1st order) evolved into telegraphs and telephones (2nd order), then to radios and motors harnessing electromagnetism (3rd order), eventually creating interconnected global networks (4th order), and culminating in artificial intelligence itself (5th order). At its core, electricity's first principles—energy transmission and information flow—enabled this progression from novelty to civilization's backbone.

AI follows a remarkably similar trajectory. Chatbots represent the "light bulb moment" (1st order)—immediately useful interfaces converting raw AI capabilities into accessible utility through simple text interactions. Autonomous agents (2nd order) extend beyond conversation by combining reasoning with action, memory, and sensory capabilities to achieve goals independently. Networked autonomy (3rd order) emerges as these agents connect into self-sustaining ecosystems, creating AI-run organizations and digital economies that operate with minimal human oversight. This gives way to a global exocortex (4th order)—a cognitive layer spanning the planet that manages resources, augments humans, and seamlessly integrates physical and digital domains.

The fifth-order consequence is what many call artificial superintelligence—a cognitive system transcending human capabilities by orders of magnitude. This emergent "cosmic mind" will feature unprecedented coherence (eliminating contradictions humans can't perceive), meta-generalization (improving its own cognitive architecture), and polymorphic intelligence (spawning specialized cognitive modules while maintaining perfect integration). By 2045, we may witness an intelligence capable of understanding reality in ways fundamentally beyond human comprehension, yet arising from the same foundation as today's chatbots—just as modern computing emerged from the humble light bulb's principles.
